key_insight: Relative to BETS, relaxed λ-(STF)₂GaCl₄ has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining substantial dimerization, and unrelaxed Wannier models reveal selectively weakened electronic connectivity.
engineering_relevance: Wannier-derived transfer integrals provide compact low-energy models for assessing how molecular substitution changes electronic coupling in organic materials.
method: Use DFT to compare BETS and STF electronic structures.
Compare DFT-selected and XRD-refined STF structures before and after fixed-lattice relaxation.
Construct two maximally localized Wannier functions per selected unrelaxed structure for the upper frontier bands.
evidence_signal: The STF structural models yield similar near-Fermi electronic structures after relaxation; unrelaxed Wannier models give t_d1 = 51 meV for BETS versus 6.5 meV for STF, with total spreads of 36.708 and 37.578 Å², respectively.
watch_item: The reported Wannier transfer integrals come from unrelaxed structures, so their quantitative applicability to relaxed structures requires verification.
paper_title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
